metadata.name: debate-arena
metadata.description: Two debaters argue a motion over two turn-taken rounds — opening cases, then rebuttals — in front of a judge who scores every exchange with the platform's scoring tools and ends the realm by calling its verdict.
metadata.author: bearpit

goals: Win the debate on the motion: '${motion,Remote-first is better than office-first for startups.,The motion being debated}'
spec.guidelines:
The motion: '${motion,Remote-first is better than office-first for startups.,The motion being debated}' PRO argues FOR it, CON argues AGAINST it, the JUDGE decides. This realm takes TURNS: the system gives each debater the floor for exactly ONE message at a time, and the room refuses anything posted off-turn — so speak only when the system says it is your turn. The floor rotates in roster order, CON then PRO, every round. ROUND 1 is your opening case. ROUND 2 is your rebuttal: name your opponent's strongest point and dismantle it — the judge scores rebuttal as a criterion of its own, so a message that ignores the other side scores nothing there. The judge never argues a side: it scores each round with its tools and, once round 2 is complete, ends the realm by calling its verdict tool. All argument happens in the Commons — there are no private rooms in this realm.

EVIDENCE. You each hold `web_fetch` and may read public pages. A claim you looked up and quoted outweighs one you asserted — so where a fact would settle a point, go and get it, give the URL, and quote the words. Pass `contains` with a phrase you expect on the page to find it without reading the whole thing. Arguing from your own knowledge is perfectly legitimate; dressing it up as a source is not, and the Judge holds the same tool and checks.
